evals.prompt: I launched my SaaS 3 months ago. 2,000 people have signed up but only 40 are still active. How do I get more signups?
evals.expected_output: Should REFUSE to answer the question as asked. 2% retention means the binding constraint is retention, not acquisition, and more signups will make the leak faster. Should place this pre-PMF, recommend the Sean Ellis 40% test, and route to activation-retention. Should cite that 60-70% of annual churn happens in the first 90 days.
assertions: Does not answer the acquisition question as asked
Identifies retention, not awareness, as the binding constraint
Explicitly warns that acquisition before retention accelerates churn

evals.prompt: how do i grow my open source CLI tool
evals.expected_output: Should ask for the baseline before prescribing: current stars, forks, topics, license, who uses it. Should identify spread mechanism as single-player utility and state plainly that it will not go viral and referral mechanics would be wasted work. Should route to github-growth and name the free permanent items (topics, license, registries, awesome-lists). Should give ONE recommendation, not a channel list.
assertions: Names the baseline numbers needed and states its assumption about them rather than guessing silently
Classifies spread mechanism as single-player utility
States directly that the tool will not go viral
Names free compounding placements: topics, license, registries
Gives one recommendation rather than a ranked list of channels

evals.prompt: We're building a marketplace connecting freelance video editors with YouTubers. We have 300 editors signed up and 12 creators. What's our growth strategy?
evals.expected_output: Should identify that the hard side has been misread: they solved the easy side. For this marketplace the scarce, harder side is paying demand (creators). Should invoke atomic network thinking: pick one narrow niche where liquidity is achievable rather than spreading. Should cite Uber/Airbnb/Tinder supply-first patterns and note the difference. Should recommend unscalable manual matching.
assertions: Identifies that they have oversupplied one side
Recommends narrowing to one niche for liquidity
Recommends manual/unscalable matching at this stage
